mainTopic: Oaths and vows to do מצוות and to learn Torah (רב גידל in the name of רב), and how to release a נידוי from a dream
overview: The גמרא brings several teachings of רב גידל in the name of רב. First, a person may swear to keep a מצוה, based on a פסוק in תהלים. The גמרא asks how that works if every Jew already swore at הר סיני. It answers that such an oath is a permitted way to motivate oneself. Next, one who commits to learn a specific פרק or מסכתא has made a 'great vow,' and here the vow really takes effect. The reason is that the basic duty of תלמוד תורה can be met with קריאת שמע morning and evening, so a specific chapter is something extra. רב גידל also teaches that whoever suggests getting up early to learn together must be the first one up, hinted at by a פסוק in יחזקאל. Then רב יוסף teaches that a נידוי received in a dream needs ten people who learned הלכה to release it, with backup options if they can't be found. רב אשי explains that the person seen in the dream cannot release the ban, because he was sent only to give it. רב אחא then asks about a dream where the person was banned and also released, and רב אשי begins answering with a comparison to grain and straw that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A source that one may swear to keep a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל in the name of רב asks for a source that a person may take a שבועה to fulfill a מצוה, and brings a פסוק from תהלים where דוד המלך says he swore to keep God's laws.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that a person may swear to do a מצוה? Because it says: 'I have sworn and I will fulfill it, to keep Your righteous laws.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב גידל in the name of רב (his first teaching here) states a rule: you are allowed to take a שבועה to do a מצוה. It brings a פסוק as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, דוד המלך says he swore to keep God's laws. That shows that swearing to do a מצוה is a proper thing to do. The next steps will ask what such an oath actually accomplishes.

phrases.english: From where do we know that one may swear to fulfill a מצוה?
As it says:
"I have sworn and I will fulfill it,
to keep Your righteous laws."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion with a source-based rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may take a שבועה to fulfill a מצוה, as shown by the פסוק 'נשבעתי ואקימה'.

steps.title: But everyone already swore at Sinai
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule: every Jew is already bound by the oath taken at הר סיני to keep the מצוות, so a new oath has nothing to take hold of.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't he already under oath from Mount Sinai?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a problem: how can a new oath to keep a מצוה mean anything, if he already swore at הר סיני to keep all the מצוות?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule that a second שבועה cannot take effect on something already covered by a first שבועה. Since the whole Jewish people swore at סיני, an oath to keep a מצוה seems to be empty. So what is the פסוק teaching?

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that...? (a challenge)
Mount Sinai, where the Jewish people accepted the Torah with an oath

phrases.english: But isn't he already under oath
from Mount Sinai?
phrases.notes: Every Jew already swore at סיני to keep all the מצוות, so a new oath seems to add nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא מוּשְׁבָּע וְעוֹמֵד מֵהַר סִינַי הוּא
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that an oath to do a מצוה is meaningful
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A שבועה cannot take effect where one is already bound by the oath of סיני, so the oath in Step 1 seems to accomplish nothing.

steps.title: The oath is a permitted way to push oneself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the teaching is not that the oath legally binds him. It is that a person may use an oath to motivate himself to do the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what it teaches us: a person is allowed to motivate himself (with such an oath).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The oath is not about creating a new legal obligation. It is a permitted way to encourage yourself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא agrees that the oath does not legally take effect, because of the oath at סיני. Still, the פסוק shows that saying such an oath is allowed and even good, because it pushes a person to act. So the point of the teaching moves from 'the oath works' to 'the oath is allowed as encouragement.'

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us

steps.whatToRemember: An oath to do a מצוה does not legally take effect, because of the oath at סיני. Making it is still permitted as a way to motivate oneself.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what it teaches us:
that a person is permitted
to motivate himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּשָׁרֵי לֵיהּ לְאִינִישׁ לְזָרוֹזֵי נַפְשֵׁיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 2 by reinterpreting Step 1.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The teaching says that an oath to do a מצוה legally binds the person.
steps.terutzMaskana: The oath does not bind him legally. The teaching is that he may make it to motivate himself.

steps.title: Committing to learn a chapter is a great vow
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל in the name of רב says that one who says he will get up early to learn a certain פרק or מסכתא has made a great נדר to the God of Israel.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב גידל said in the name of רב: One who says 'I will get up early and learn this chapter,' or 'I will learn this tractate,' has made a great vow to the God of Israel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second teaching of רב גידל. It praises someone who commits to learn a specific part of the Torah, and calls this a 'great vow.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'he has vowed a great vow' sound like the commitment really takes effect as a binding obligation. This sets up the next challenge, which is the same problem as before: isn't he already obligated in Torah learning?

phrases.english: And Rav Giddel said in the name of Rav:
One who says, "I will get up early and learn this chapter,"
or "I will learn this tractate"
has vowed a great vow
to the God of Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַב הָאוֹמֵר אַשְׁכִּים וְאֶשְׁנֶה פֶּרֶק זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching from the same speaker, on a related theme.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A commitment to learn a specific פרק or מסכתא is a great נדר to the God of Israel.

steps.title: He is already bound to learn Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: he is already under oath to learn Torah, and a שבועה cannot take effect on an existing שבועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't he already under oath? And an oath does not take effect on another oath!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises the same problem as before. Learning Torah is already a מצוה he swore to keep at סיני, so how can this vow take effect?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule is אין שבועה חלה על שבועה: a second oath cannot land on something an earlier oath already covers. Since תלמוד תורה is part of the oath at סיני, the 'great vow' seems to have nothing to add.

keyTerms.meaning: An oath cannot take effect on something already covered by an oath

phrases.english: But isn't he already under oath?
phrases.notes: He means the oath of סיני, which includes the מצוה of learning Torah.

phrases.english: And an oath does not take effect on an oath!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא מוּשְׁבָּע וְעוֹמֵד הוּא וְאֵין שְׁבוּעָה חָלָה עַל שְׁבוּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 4 in the same way Step 2 challenged Step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the vow to learn is a real ('great') vow
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Learning Torah is already sworn at סיני, and אין שבועה חלה על שבועה, so the vow cannot take effect.

steps.title: If it is just motivation, it repeats the first teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks the earlier answer: if רב גידל only means that one may vow to motivate oneself, that is already his first teaching. So what is new here?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us? That even just for motivation it is allowed? That is the same as רב גידל's first teaching!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes further. It cannot use the same answer as before ('it's just for motivation'), because then this second teaching would just repeat the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Steps 1–3, the answer was that such an oath is allowed as a way to motivate oneself. If the second teaching meant only that, it would add nothing new. So the second teaching must be saying something different, probably that this vow really does take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? (What is new here?)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is rejecting the first teaching here. It is only saying the second teaching must mean something different from the first.

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
That even merely to motivate oneself (it is allowed)?
That is the same as Rav Giddel's first teaching!
phrases.notes: This points back to Steps 1–3, where the oath was explained as a way to push oneself.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דַּאֲפִילּוּ זָרוֹזֵי בְּעָלְמָא הַיְינוּ דְּרַב גִּידֵּל קַמַּיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the challenge of Step 5 by blocking the answer used in Step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using the 'motivation' answer to explain the second teaching
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the second teaching only meant motivation, it would be a repeat of the first teaching, and a teacher does not say the same thing twice.

steps.title: שמע covers the basic duty, so the vow takes hold
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the vow really does take effect. A person can fulfill the basic מצוה of תלמוד תורה with קריאת שמע morning and evening, so learning a specific chapter is beyond what he already swore.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it teaches us: since, if he wants, he can exempt himself with קריאת שמע morning and evening, therefore the oath does take effect on him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer. The vow to learn a specific פרק is binding, because it goes beyond the minimum obligation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic obligation of learning Torah can be met just by saying קריאת שמע שחרית וערבית. So the oath of סיני does not require him to learn this particular chapter. Because the vow covers something extra, it is not an 'oath on an oath,' and it takes effect.
steps.whatToRemember: An oath to do a מצוה usually cannot take effect, and is only allowed as a way to motivate oneself. A vow to learn a specific פרק or מסכתא does take effect, because קריאת שמע morning and evening already fulfills the minimum duty of תלמוד תורה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a general idea: a שבועה can take effect on the part of a מצוה that goes beyond the minimum required.

phrases.english: This is what it teaches us:
Since, if he wants,
he can exempt himself with the recitation of Shema
phrases.notes: Exempt from the basic obligation of learning Torah. Saying שמע is enough for the minimum.

phrases.english: morning and evening,
because of that, the oath takes effect on him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן כֵּיוָן דְּאִי בָּעֵי פָּטַר נַפְשֵׁיהּ בִּקְרִיַּת שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenges of Steps 5 and 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the existing obligation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The vow to learn falls under the oath of סיני and cannot take effect, or it is merely for motivation.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since קריאת שמע fulfills the minimum duty, learning a specific chapter is extra, so the vow truly takes effect.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A vow to learn a specific פרק or מסכתא is binding, because it goes beyond the minimum obligation of תלמוד תורה.

steps.title: Whoever suggests learning early must get up first
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל in the name of רב teaches that if someone says to a friend, 'Let us get up early and learn this chapter,' he is the one who must get up early. A פסוק in יחזקאל hints at this.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גידל said in the name of רב: If someone tells his friend, 'Let's get up early and learn this chapter,' he has to be the one who gets up early. As the פסוק says: 'He said to me: Get up, go out to the valley, and there I will speak with you. I went out to the valley, and ה׳'s glory was already standing there.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching from רב גידל about getting up early to learn. This time it is about two friends who plan to learn together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person who makes the plan has to be there first. The proof is that ה׳ invited יחזקאל to the valley, and when יחזקאל arrived, ה׳'s glory was already there waiting.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a practical lesson about learning with a partner: whoever invites should also be the first one ready.

phrases.english: Rav Giddel said in the name of Rav:
One who says to his friend
"Let us get up early and learn this chapter"
— it is on him to get up early,
as it says:
"And He said to me (son of man):
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets, and the פסוק itself doesn't have them here.

phrases.english: Get up, go out to the valley,
and there I will speak with you.
And I went out to the valley,
and behold, the glory of ה׳ was standing there."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַב: הָאוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third teaching from רב גידל in the name of רב, on the related theme of getting up early to learn.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The one who suggests learning early together is the one who must get up early, as hinted in יחזקאל 3:22–23.

steps.title: A ban from a dream needs ten learned people to release it
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף teaches that a person put under נידוי in a dream needs ten people to release it. They should be people who learned הלכה, but if none are available, people who only recited משנה are enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: If someone was put under נידוי in a dream, he needs ten people to release it. They must be people who have learned הלכה. People who only recited משנה without learning הלכה don't qualify. But if there aren't ten who learned הלכה, then even people who only recited משנה can do it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: what to do if someone dreams that he was put under נידוי. רב יוסף says ten people are needed to release it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not just any ten people qualify. The first choice is people who have learned הלכה. If they can't be found, people who only recited משנה are accepted as a backup.

keyTerms.meaning: A ban; being pushed away from the community
They recited (the text of the משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up תָּנוּ and מַתְנוּ. Here תָּנוּ הִלְכְתָא means they really learned הלכה, while מַתְנוּ וְלָא תָּנוּ means they only recited משנה. The first group is preferred.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
If they put him under a ban in a dream,

phrases.aramaic: צָרִיךְ עֲשָׂרָה בְּנֵי אָדָם לְהַתִּיר לוֹ,
phrases.english: he needs ten people to release it for him,
and that is only if they have learned הלכה,
but if they recited משנה and did not learn הלכה — no.
And if there are none who learned הלכה,
— even people who recited and did not learn will do.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic connected to the general theme of נדרים and bans.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dream-נידוי needs ten people to release it. People who learned הלכה come first, and people who only recited משנה are a backup.

steps.title: If no qualified ten are around, wait at the crossroads
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף continues: if even those are not available, the person should sit at a crossroads and greet people until ten who learned הלכה happen to pass by.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if there aren't even those, he should go sit at a crossroads and greet people with שלום, until ten people who have learned הלכה happen to come by.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a last backup plan for someone who can't find any qualified group of ten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even in the worst case, the release still has to be done by ten people who learned הלכה. The crossroads just makes it more likely that such people will pass by, so he greets travelers until he finds them.

phrases.english: And if there are none,
phrases.notes: Meaning there aren't even ten who recited משנה.

phrases.english: let him go and sit at a crossroads
and give greetings of שלום to ten people,
until there happen to come to him
ten who have learned הלכה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי לֵיכָּא לֵיזִיל וְלִיתֵּב אַפָּרָשַׁת דְּרָכִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב יוסף's teaching with a final backup plan.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If no qualified ten can be found, he should wait at a crossroads, greeting people, until ten who learned הלכה come by.

steps.title: Can the person from the dream release the ban himself?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי: if the dreamer knows who banned him in the dream, can that person release him?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא asked רב אשי: If he knows who put him under the ban in the dream, can that person release it for him?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא asks a question about רב יוסף's rule. Maybe ten people aren't needed if the dreamer recognizes the one who banned him. This sets up רב אשי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, the one who made a ban can also undo it. So רבינא wonders whether the person seen in the dream could release it alone, without ten people.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
If he knows who banned him in the dream,
what is the law, can that person release it for him?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: יָדַע מַאן שַׁמְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a specific case under רב יוסף's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the person who banned him in the dream can release the ban alone, instead of ten people.

steps.title: He was sent only to ban, not to release
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the person in the dream was made a messenger only to ban him, not to release him, so ten people are still needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to him: They made him a messenger to ban him. They did not make him a messenger to release him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers רבינא's question: no, the person from the dream cannot release the ban.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person seen in the dream was only a messenger from Heaven, and his job was limited to giving the ban. He has no power to undo it, so רב יוסף's rule of ten people stays in place.
steps.whatToRemember: A נידוי from a dream is released by ten people who learned הלכה, with backups if needed. The person seen in the dream cannot release it, because he was only sent to give the ban.

phrases.english: He said to him:
To ban him, they made him a messenger,
phrases.notes: "They" means Heaven, which sent this person in the dream.

phrases.english: to release him, they did not make him a messenger.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. The dream figure was only a messenger to ban, not to release, so ten people are still required.

steps.title: Banned and released in the same dream
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא asks רב אשי: if a person was banned and then also released inside his dream, what is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא said to רב אשי: If they put him under a ban and then released him, all in his dream, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא asks רב אשי a new question about dream-bans: what if the release also happened in the dream?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we assumed the dream had only a ban, so a real-life release by ten people was needed. Here the dream itself seems to 'fix' the problem by including a release. רב אחא wants to know whether that dream-release counts, or whether he still needs ten people.

keyTerms.meaning: They put him under נידוי (a ban)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha said to Rav Ashi:
If they banned him and released him in his dream, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבינא asked about the person who banned him in the dream, רב אחא asks about a dream that contained the release too.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a release that happens in the same dream cancel a dream-ban, or are ten people still required?

steps.title: רב אשי begins: grain always comes with straw
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי starts his answer with a comparison: just as grain cannot grow without straw...
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to him: Just as it is impossible for grain to grow without straw...
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי begins answering with a comparison, and this line is only the first half. It sets up the point he finishes in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grain always grows together with straw, which is useless and thrown away. רב אשי is preparing to say that dreams also mix meaningful parts with meaningless parts. So he is hinting that not everything in a dream should be taken seriously, and the rest of the comparison comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Straw (the useless part of the stalk)

phrases.english: He said to him: Just as it is impossible
for grain to be without straw,
phrases.notes: Here בָּר means grain, not 'son'. The sentence finishes in the next line.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לַבָּר בְּלֹא תֶּבֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב אשי begins answering רב אחא's question from step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Opening half of an analogy: grain always comes mixed with useless straw. The conclusion about dreams is completed in the next line.
